title: Broomstick lace slouchy beanie
excerpt: A slouchy beanie worked in aran yarn using broomstick lace. The petal clusters give a bold open texture and the brim is worked in double crochet ribbing for a snug fit.
sourceNotes: A hat with a ribbed brim worked flat then seamed, and a broomstick lace body joined at the sides. Clusters of 5 give a generous lace texture.

glossaryTerms.definition: A ribbed fabric made by working double crochet into the back loop only on every row. This creates a stretchy, ribbed brim that hugs the head.
Closing the top of a hat by threading yarn through the final row of stitches, pulling tight, and fastening securely.

crochet.gaugeText: 3 clusters (15 sts) x 4 rows = 10 cm in broomstick lace on 5.0 mm hook.

content.text: brim, then switches to broomstick lace for the body. The crown is closed with a
Chain 10. Row 1: dc in 2nd ch from hook and each ch (9 dc). Turn. Row 2: ch 1, dc in back loop of each dc. Turn. Repeat row 2 until the brim strip measures 56 cm. Seam the short ends together.

Work 60 dc evenly around the top edge of the brim. Do not turn. Draw up a loop from each stitch onto the dowel (60 loops). Slide 5 loops off, ch 1, work 5 dc through centre; repeat across (12 clusters). Repeat loop and cluster rows for 15 cm.
Thread the yarn through the tapestry needle and run it through every final stitch. Pull tight to close the crown and fasten off. Weave in all ends.
